items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
items.why: The binding EU rule and source of the six-month figure. Use in accordance with the instructions for use; input data relevant and sufficiently representative 'to the extent the deployer exercises control' over it; monitoring; suspension and notification where a risk appears; logs kept 'to the extent such logs are under their control' and 'unless provided otherwise' in other law, including data protection law. High-risk systems only. Commission's copy of the consolidated text, stated on the page to be based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026, with Digital Omnibus changes marked NEW or AMENDED.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 13: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use
items.why: What the instructions must contain: intended purpose, the level of accuracy to be expected, known circumstances that affect it, human oversight measures and how to collect and interpret logs. Defines the limits inside which the provider's assurances hold. Commission's copy of the consolidated text, stated on the page to be based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026, with Digital Omnibus changes marked NEW or AMENDED.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 25: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: they modify the intended purpose of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which has not been classified as high-risk
items.why: The consequence of using a system outside its intended purpose: a deployer whose change makes it high-risk is treated as the provider and takes on the provider's obligations. Commission's copy of the consolidated text, stated on the page to be based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026, with Digital Omnibus changes marked NEW or AMENDED.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 113: Entry into force and application
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.locator: Art. 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i), marked AMENDED
items.quote: Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from:
items.why: Source of the date in the brief: Article 26 sits in Chapter III Section 3, which applies from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I products. The page footer still says 'Official version of 13 June 2024'; the banner and AMENDED markers were relied on. Commission's copy of the consolidated text, stated on the page to be based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026, with Digital Omnibus changes marked NEW or AMENDED.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 99: Penalties
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: obligations of deployers pursuant to Article 26
items.why: Breach of the deployer obligations falls in the tier of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 3 % of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. Member States set the rules; not used as the brief's figure. Commission's copy of the consolidated text, stated on the page to be based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026, with Digital Omnibus changes marked NEW or AMENDED.

items.title: Guidance on AI and data protection: What do we need to know about accuracy and statistical accuracy?
items.locator: Section on statistical accuracy after deployment (paragraph beginning 'As part of your obligation to implement data protection by design and by default'); passage on concept or model drift
items.quote: The higher the impact the more frequently you should monitor and report on it.
items.why: Source of the quotation. The UK regulator's expectation of monitoring after deployment, scaled to the effect on people, with documented thresholds for retraining and attention to drift; it applies equally where the system is bought in. Guidance, where personal data is processed. Marked under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

items.title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.locator: Principle 12 'Monitor your system’s behaviour', provisions 12.1-12.4; definition of 'System Operators'
items.quote: System Operators shall log system and user actions to support security compliance, incident investigations, and vulnerability remediation.
items.why: The UK government's own statement on logging and monitoring by organisations that deploy AI ('System Operators'). Voluntary, and framed around security, not fairness. Sets no retention period.

items.title: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks
items.publisher: Bank of England, Prudential Regulation Authority
items.locator: Principle 2.6 'Use of externally developed models, third-party vendor products', points (a) and (b), PDF p.19
items.quote: validate their own use of vendor products and conduct ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis of vendor model performance using their own outcomes
items.why: A UK regulator's version of the deployer's duty: responsibility stays with the firm when a model is bought in, vendor data and assumptions are checked, and the firm monitors against its own results. Banks with internal model approval only.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.locator: MANAGE 3.1, Table 4, p.32; MEASURE 2.4, Table 3, p.29; MANAGE 4.1, Table 4, p.33
items.quote: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.
items.why: International comparator for monitoring bought-in AI in production and for post-deployment monitoring plans, including override and decommissioning. Voluntary, United States.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in UK financial services - 2024
items.publisher: Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority
items.quote: 46% of respondent firms reported having only ‘partial understanding’ of the AI technologies they use
items.why: Source of the second figure, and evidence for the gap this question tests: the report attributes partial understanding largely to third-party models. Regulated financial firms only; self-reported; 118 responses.
